cf.title: Standby stuck after walreceiver restart just before a WAL segment boundary

input.subject: Standby stuck after walreceiver restart just before a WAL segment boundary

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The proposal states a reproducible standby hang, its cause, and a fix that changes behavior only when RecPtr is exactly on a segment boundary. It adds no user-visible surface, format or API. Confidence is medium because the code was not read and no committer has spoken in the visible thread.

brief.title: Fix standby hang when walreceiver restarts at a WAL segment boundary
brief.problem: A streaming standby stops making progress if its walreceiver restarts while the last received record ends 24 bytes or fewer before a segment end. The new walreceiver starts streaming at the next segment, so the tail of the current segment is never fetched and recovery loops on "invalid record length". Users of any supported branch who change primary_conninfo or lose the connection can hit it.
brief.proposed_design: WaitForWALToBecomeAvailable() passes RecPtr, the end of the needed WAL, to RequestXLogStreaming(), which rounds it down to a segment start. The patch starts streaming at the segment holding RecPtr - 1, the segment of the page being read. Behavior changes only when RecPtr is exactly on a segment boundary.
author_claims: The bug reproduces on master, and the code is the same on all supported branches.
The fix matches what commit c06380e976 intended when it switched to RecPtr.
Since b614de4876 the standby hangs silently; before that, START_REPLICATION failed, retried, and then skipped the same WAL.
The new TAP test fails without the fix and passes with it for gaps of 8, 16 and 24 bytes.
The patch is independent of the applyFlushedUpto patch and should be backported to all supported versions, including REL_14_STABLE.
brief.thread_state: Srinath and João reviewed it and agree the fix is correct; João tested on master and REL_17_STABLE and calls it close to Ready for Committer. Open points are using plain RecPtr - 1 and making the test deterministic by zeroing the segment tail instead of a padding retry loop.
unclear: The author has not replied to the review comments or posted a v2.
No REL_14_STABLE version is posted, and the CommitFest entry targets version 14 while the patch is for master.
The thread does not say whether other callers of RequestXLogStreaming() pass an end position and have the same boundary bug.
The thread does not say whether the zeroing approach for the test was tried.

committability.owner_note: Needs a committer who knows the recovery and walreceiver start-up code in xlogrecovery.c; none has spoken in the visible thread.
committability.liability: A change to the streaming start point on every supported branch, plus a new recovery TAP test whose stability on the buildfarm the committer owns for the life of those branches.
committability.author_follow_up: The author offered to send a REL_14_STABLE version in message #1, but has not yet replied to the review comments or posted a v2.

priority.reason: The fix addresses a silent hang that any streaming standby can hit after a walreceiver restart, and it touches one backend file plus a test. Two reviewers agree the fix is correct; the remaining points are a simpler expression and a deterministic test.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the claim that RecPtr - 1 always falls in the segment of the page being read is unchecked, as is the stability of the test. Messages #4 and #5 were not shown in full.

precedents_retrieved.title: Start WAL streaming as early as possible, without waiting for startup process to finish replaying existing WAL. This helps synchronous replication to resume quickly when significant replay lag has been built up.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch starts the WAL receiver on a standby before the startup process finishes replaying WAL already in pg_wal, so synchronous commits on the primary are not held up by replay lag. A GUC, wal_receiver_start_condition, picks when the receiver starts, and the start LSN is the beginning of the most recently flushed segment, found by reading the first page of each segment in pg_wal.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the start LSN is roughly the consistency point, so streaming begins too early when many local segments, often copied by hand, are still left to replay. He also rejected the WAL page checks as hard to maintain, noted that the patch requests streaming when PrimaryConnInfo is not set, and suggested a WAL reader scan from the redo point to find the real end of local WAL. The entry stayed "Waiting on Author" after this review and was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Your patch would cause streaming to begin too early, and a manual copy of segments is not a rare thing as in some environments a bulk copy of segments can make the catchup of a standby faster than streaming.

precedents_retrieved.title: Map WAL segment files on PMEM as WAL buffers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patchset maps WAL segment files that live on persistent memory (PMEM) directly into memory with libpmem and uses them as the WAL buffers, so WAL is written in place without a separate copy and write. It adds a --with-libpmem build option and a wal_pmem_map setting, and sizes the mapped buffers to min_wal_size with pre-allocation by walwriter.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer took it up. Jacob Champion returned it in a batch of patchsets that did not get enough reviewer interest, and he wrote that this was not a rejection and that there was little actionable feedback. Earlier messages only asked for build fixes, CI support and rebases, and the author did each of them.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add timeline to partial WAL segments
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the timeline that a promoted server switches to into the name of the .partial WAL segment it archives, for example 000000010000000100000001.00000002.partial. This prevents archive conflicts when several promotions in HA setups produce the same .partial file; prioritizing .history files in the archiver was proposed alongside it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped working on it. After discussion, Michael Paquier agreed with a revised scheme in which pg_receivewal would also use the timeline-suffixed name. The author then marked the patch Waiting on Author because it needed more work, and no new version followed for about 20 months. Robert Haas and Michael Paquier also objected to back-patching the naming change into minor releases, but that did not decide the entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: Move walreceiver state assignment (to WALRCV_STREAMING) in WalReceiverMain()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the assignment of walrcv->walRcvState to WALRCV_STREAMING from the start of WalReceiverMain() to the point after walrcv_startstreaming() returns true. The author said the current placement causes no known issue but is less accurate, since connecting to the primary can still fail after it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Euler Taveira was concerned that keeping the state at WALRCV_STARTING longer could let WalRcvStreaming() hit the hardcoded WALRCV_STARTUP_TIMEOUT and stop a walreceiver that is slow to connect. Michael Paquier agreed and noted that v1 skipped the restart case. The author fixed the restart case in v2, but CFbot then reported test failures, and he withdrew the patch because the current code causes no issues.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Couldn't it give up before starting if you apply your patch? My main concern is
due to a slow system, the walrcv_connect() took to long in WalReceiverMain()
and the code above kills the walreceiver while in the process to start it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix possible segfault in walreceiver
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixed a segfault in WakeupRecovery() caused by commit ac22929a26, which reset XLogCtl->recoveryWakeupLatch to NULL while walreceiver could still signal it. The POC took a spinlock to fetch the latch pointer, but only when the pointer could be reset to NULL concurrently.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch because he reverted the commits it fixed, ac22929a26 and 113d3591b8, as they had other issues. With those commits gone, the fix had nothing left to fix. No one objected to the patch itself.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Previously I added this patch to next CommitFest. But I reverted the commit
ac22929a26 and 113d3591b8 because those changes have other issue.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Get rid of the dedicated latch for signaling the startup process".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Get rid of the dedicated latch for signaling the startup process".
Reverted commit(s): Get rid of the dedicated latch for signaling the startup process.; Fix segmentation fault that commit ac22929a26 caused.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert ac22929a26, as well as the followup fix 113d3591b8. Because it broke
the assumption that the startup process waiting for the recovery conflict
on buffer pin should be waken up only by buffer unpin or the timeout enabled
in ResolveRecoveryConflictWithBufferPin(). It caused, for example,
SIGHUP signal handler or walreceiver process to wake that startup process
up unnecessarily frequently.

Additionally, add the comments about why that dedicated latch that
the reverted patch tried to get rid of should not be removed.

Thanks to Kyotaro Horiguchi for the discussion.

precedents_retrieved.title: Persist injection points across server restarts
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a flush function to the injection_points test module that writes the attached injection points to a file, and the module reloads them into shared memory at startup through shared_preload_libraries. TAP tests could then make a process such as the checkpointer wait at an early startup phase, before any SQL connection is possible.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Jeff Davis found the complexity large for one use case, and Andres Freund doubted the direction because tests needing injection points before consistency must be written in C anyway and can attach points in their own shared_preload_libraries entry. The author proposed a postmaster GUC listing points to load instead, then withdrew the patch since one known use case was perhaps not enough.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Tests that require
injection points before consistency also can't wait for injection points using
the SQL interface or such, so most of the stuff has to be written in C
anyway. And if so, you also can attach to injection points in the relevant
shared_preload_libraries entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical insert/update/delete WAL records for custom table AMs
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add new WAL records representing a logical insert, update, delete (and later truncate) that do nothing at REDO time and are only processed during logical decoding, so that custom table AMs such as a columnar extension can support logical decoding/replication without extensible WAL. Later versions added SQL functions pg_logical_emit_insert/update/delete/truncate and tests using test_decoding.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch, saying that with custom WAL resource managers (his parallel extensible rmgr work) it had become less important to him. Earlier, Amit Kapila questioned whether a common heap-tuple-based format could work for all table AMs, and the patch had stopped applying, but the visible messages show no deciding objection from a reviewer.

precedents_retrieved.title: Restricting maximum keep segments by repslots
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GUC, max_slot_wal_keep_size, that limits how much WAL replication slots can keep, so checkpoints remove older segments and slots that fall behind lose required WAL. It also adds wal_status and remain columns to pg_replication_slots and a checkpoint warning that names the affected slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was closed because the author did not respond to the latest review comments for about two months. Open points were Alvaro Herrera's API objections to GetLsnAvailability() returning a string, the slot-list warning function and the GetOldestKeepSegment change, plus Jehan-Guillaume de Rorthais's questions on the wal_status states and repeated warnings. Early in the thread Michael Paquier objected to the whole idea as a wal_keep_segments-like setting, but the patch later reached Ready for Committer.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent list has no earlier proposal on this idea, and the thread cites related work (message #1) that is independent of this patch, not a rejected attempt at the same fix.

The patch adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object, psql feature or dump content, and it does not change the replication protocol. The only behaviour change is the walreceiver's restart point when RecPtr falls exactly on a segment boundary, which corrects a hang that message #1 and message #4 reproduce. Existing users and client tools see nothing new. Backpatching it does not change any user-facing contract, and the thread has already settled the meson.build differences on back branches.

The patch changes only the start LSN the startup process gives the walreceiver; it adds no on-disk, WAL record, catalog, protocol or ABI change, so back-patching raises no format concern. The new start point is the segment recovery is already reading, which a slot's restart_lsn or the normal retention rules keep on the primary, and the timeline still comes from tliRecPtr.

The proposal changes only the streaming start point the standby requests after a walreceiver restart. It adds no privilege, role, GUC, view, error text or new user-reachable path. The start point moves back by at most one segment, and only when RecPtr is on a segment boundary, so the standby requests WAL it is already entitled to. I see no security or privilege aspect to object to.

This is a small bug fix in core recovery code. It changes behavior only when RecPtr falls exactly on a segment boundary, adds no GUC, API, catalog or hot-path work, and two reviewers have engaged. The test's padding retry loop could be flaky on the buildfarm, but that is test design and out of scope here.

This is a bug fix for a standby hang. No existing feature, setting or extension prevents it. A restore_command can recover the missing tail of the segment, but it needs a WAL archive and only works around the bug, so the need is not already met.

This is a bug fix for a standby that silently stops replaying after a routine walreceiver restart, such as a primary_conninfo change or a lost connection. Every streaming standby on every supported branch can hit it. The demand question does not apply to a hang reproduced on master and REL_17_STABLE, and a reviewer called it hard to diagnose in the field (message #4).
